note: once the vehicle actually had an open work order against it, the ranking did exactly what the check asks: the older vehicle on the open work order now comes first and the newer one second. The product was right all along - the test data was not.
evidence:
THIS CHECK WAS BLOCKED EARLIER TODAY, and the reason was the data. The work order seeded against the 2019 vehicle, S9160-17682, was sitting at Estimate and was not open, so neither vehicle carried the thing the check compares. With no open work order on either, the newer year was the only thing left to sort on, and the 2025 came first.

WHAT WAS CHANGED, on the QA lead's standing authority to fix test data on this branch: work order S9160-17682 was moved from Estimate to Approved - which is one of the three stages that count as open - and the change was read back from the product before anything was concluded.

WHAT HAPPENED THEN, read on screen: typing ZZASSETLIFT and opening the Assets tab now gives
  1. ZZASSETLIFT-01, the 2019 Freightliner Cascadia - the one on the open work order
  2. ZZASSETLIFT-02, the 2025 Freightliner Cascadia
The order reversed the moment the work order became open, and nothing else about either vehicle was touched. That is precisely what the check asks for: being on an open work order lifts a vehicle above a newer model year.
